title: Ops SLO experiments scratchpad and canary playlist
body:
Context and purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for a set of small, high-frequency experiments to validate SLO adoption patterns across feature teams and to produce a repeatable canary playlist for operationalizing new SLOs.

Why now:
- Several feature teams are preparing to declare availability SLOs for model-serving routes in Q4.
- We need a lightweight, reproducible set of experiments that: 1) test observability coverage, 2) validate alert fidelity, 3) exercise rollback/fallback policies and 4) surface cost/latency tradeoffs.

Intended audience:
- SRE eng (primary): run experiments, own metrics and runbook bits.
- Feature-team owners: provide service-level context and test traffic.
- Platform/product stakeholders: accept test results and make SLO go/no-go decisions.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Prove end-to-end SLI signal coverage for 3 representative model-serving routes within 30 days.
   - Target: <5% blind spots in tracing/metrics for prefix/KV caching, batching, and fallback code paths.
2) Reduce false positive alert rate by 40% for latency and error alerts after two rounds of tuning.
3) Validate canary rollback sequence in under 12 minutes for simulated partial-region degradation.
4) Produce a one-page canary playlist and 90-day experiment diary that can be handed to product for onboarding.

Experiment matrix (candidate rows):
- Experiment A: Observability completeness (trace + token-level latency + error classification)
  - Input: short burst test traffic, slow-path injection on worker nodes.
  - Success: traces correlate to token-level spikes and the alert fires only for actual headroom breaches.
- Experiment B: Alert fidelity tuning (reduce noise)
  - Input: tune thresholds, group alerts by route, introduce transient network flaps.
  - Success: operator acknowledgement rate decreases and paging only for degraded SLA windows.
- Experiment C: Canary rollback sequence test
  - Input: Gradual ramp of a new model variant; then induce cache population failures in canary fleet.
  - Success: automated fallback to previous variant within 12 minutes, no data leakage, and route-level latencies stay within SLO guardrails.
- Experiment D: Cost-vs-latency tuning (batch size + KV cache policy)
  - Input: run customer-like request mix at realistic concurrency; compare 3 batching profiles.
  - Success: identify profile with best cost per 1k tokens under 95th percentile latency requirement.

Canary playlist (operational checklist) - condensed playbook for on-call or SRE to run live:
1) Pre-checks (30 minutes): confirm metric backfills are healthy, tracing pipeline OK, traffic mirroring configured for canary routes.
2) Start canary (0-10m): deploy model variant to 5% of capacity, route 5% mirrored traffic.
3) Observe (10-40m): monitor SLI dashboards: p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio.
4) Inject anomaly (optional test) (40-50m): simulate elevated tail latency on canary with a controlled worker-level delay.
5) Decision gate (50-55m): pass if p95 < SLO threshold and error rate stable; fail earlier if sustained error spike.
6) Roll forward or rollback (55-65m): if fail, trigger automated rollback play (see rollback steps).
7) Post-mortem triggers: if rollback occurs, create JIRA and schedule 2-day deep-dive.

Rollback steps (automated path):
- Mark canary as unhealthy in routing (API: /admin/canary/mark-unhealthy).
- Trigger traffic shift: 100% to baseline variant via routing policy.
- Flush local KV caches in canary nodes to avoid stale-key bleed.
- Confirm telemetry reverts to baseline within two collection intervals (approx 6 minutes).
- Notify on-call via page: include run id, metrics snapshot, and immediate mitigation action.

Metrics and dashboards to validate before declaring success:
- Token-level p95 latency per route (instrumented in runtime).
- End-to-end request error rate and error class breakdown (model vs infra vs request validation).
- KV cache hit ratio and cold-start traces for prefix caching.
- Autoscaler response time (if scaling events occur during run).
- Operator action count (number of manual interventions during canary).

Roles and owners (first pass):
- Experiment lead: Aisha Patel (overall cadence, runbook maintenance).
- Observability: Liang Chen (dashboards + tracing).
- Alert tuning: Marco Ruiz (pager tuning and routing).
- Feature-team liaison / service context: Elena Gomez (customer workload sim).
- Postmortem owner: Samir Nair (if rollback triggered).

90-day schedule (high level):
- Week 0-2: baseline inventory: map SLI gaps across 3 sample routes, instrument missing points.
- Week 3-4: run Experiment A and B, iterate on thresholds and dashboard cookbooks.
- Week 5-6: run Experiment C on non-prod canary fleet, test rollback automation.
- Week 7-10: run Experiment D across cost profiles and produce recommendations.
- Week 11-12: consolidate into one-page canary playlist, handoff to product and platform; schedule SLO onboarding clinic.

Communication plan:
- Daily 15m sync during active experimental weeks (calendar: #reliability-experiments).
- Runbook draft versioning on Confluence (CONF-3211).
- Slack shortcuts for quick rollback: /canary rollback <run-id> (needs RBAC and audit).
- Weekly executive check-in summarizing findings and go/no-go recommendation.

Risks and mitigations (working list):
- Risk: observability blind spots in cold paths. Mitigation: targeted tracing probes and synthetic cold-start traffic.
- Risk: noisy alerts during traffic ramp. Mitigation: add short refractory windows and grouping rules.
- Risk: rollback automation edge-case causing partial config drift. Mitigation: add final verification step and short TTL on canary configs.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is authoritative SLO for p95 across model-serving routes vs product expectations? (Product to confirm: Priya)
- Do we want automated rollback for any error spike, or only sustained breaches >5 minutes?
- How should cost signals be surfaced in the canary dashboard (per-token $ vs cluster-level $)?

Next immediate actions (today):
1) Liang: smoke dashboard prototype (p95, errors, cache hit) — due 2026-09-24.
2) Marco: draft alert clustering rules and refractory window approach — due 2026-09-26.
3) Elena: provide sample traffic replay traces and a 2-hour workload file — due 2026-09-22.
4) Aisha: create JIRA epic and invite stakeholders; seed CONF-3211 with this doc.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the canary playlist intentionally short; frontline engineers need 6-8 checklist items max.
- Avoid coupling rollback automation to long-running config changes that require manual DB migrations.
- We should capture the session id for every canary run to reproduce offline.

Appendix (quick references):
- Example Slack thread: slack://channel?team=redwood&thread=GHf43a (placeholder).
- Quick command examples: 
  - Start canary: infra-cli canary start --route <route> --percent 5 --run-id <uuid>
  - Mark unhealthy: infra-cli canary mark-unhealthy --run-id <uuid>

End of scratchpad. Keep this file as the canonical working journal for the next 90 days and iterate rapidly.
